transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Lena Kovács (CTO, Mistral Labs), Samir Patel (ML Eng), Priya Singh (Security)

Summary (auto): quickstart questions, hosted vs dedicated discussion, security checklist, next steps to provision trial credits and run pilot.

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, I'm Ava with Redwood. Diego from our SE team is here. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Lena: Good, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in. We're looking to evaluate a hosted API first, maybe move to dedicated later. Main goal is fast time to first token for our engineers.
[00:22] Diego: Great. We'll cover the PLG quickstart flow, how free credits work, SDKs, and then high-level differences between hosted, dedicated and private. Happy to deep dive on latency/cost tradeoffs after.
[00:35] Samir: Perfect. Our constraints: HIPAA-ish data on some flows later, but for initial proof of concept it's okay to use hosted. We care about latency under 200ms p50 for short prompts and cost per 1k tokens.
[00:50] Priya: And from security, we need SOC 2, SSO/SAML, and KMS integration eventually. Also audit logs and retention controls.
[01:05] Ava: Totally, all common asks. For quickstart, we can spin up a trial org, give free credits (usually 100-200 USD equivalent depending on offer), you get API keys and our SDKs. Time-to-first-token for a developer using the SDK is often <15 minutes if you follow the quickstart.
[01:28] Lena: Nice. Is that self-serve? We want to let our engineers poke around without a full procurement cycle.
[01:35] Ava: Yes, PLG self-serve. Sign-up, verify email, create org, and we can pre-provision credits for your domain. The SDKs are in Python/Node and there's a simple cURL example. Diego, do you want to show the example quickly?
[01:48] Diego: Sure. The example is basically import redwood, set API_KEY environment variable, then client.generate with model name. cURL is a one-liner using Authorization: Bearer token. We also support streaming responses via SSE or chunked HTTP.
[02:05] Samir: Are sample code snippets in the console?
[02:08] Diego: Yep, in the Console under Quickstart, you can copy Python/Node/cURL. We also surface per-route latency and cost once you start sending real requests.
[02:18] Priya: For the SOC 2 docs, can you share them? Also our security team will want detail on data at rest encryption and customer-managed keys.
[02:26] Ava: Absolutely. We'll send the security pack with SOC 2, SSO guide, and KMS options. For hosted, we offer KMS integrations so you can bring-your-own-key in some plans, and Private/VPC supports HSM integrations for on-prem.
[02:41] Lena: Good to know. On the model side, are you hosting open models or proprietary? We want specific latency profiles for the models you recommend.
[02:50] Diego: We host a mix of curated open models and optimized variants. We publish performance profiles — typical p50/p95 numbers — but these depend on prompt length and batching. For PLG, you can pick a model from the catalog and try it; for Dedicated we can pin versions and give more predictable throughput.
[03:12] Samir: About Dedicated: what's the rough commit sizes and how long to onboard?
[03:18] Ava: Dedicated is usually monthly or annual reserved capacity with GPU pools. Commit size varies — we can tailor it. Onboarding depends on scale but plan a couple weeks for provisioning and tests. For early evaluation, hosted is fastest.
[03:35] Priya: If we later need Private (VPC/on-prem), how does that affect the quickstart?
[03:40] Diego: Private is a separate install path and requires more lead time, network setup, and security review. It doesn't block the quickstart — you can start on hosted and then plan a migration. We support canary rollouts and A/B traffic during transitions.
[03:55] Lena: Great. Can we do a small bench on hosted to validate latency before committing?
[03:59] Diego: Yes. We can provision a test org, give you credits, and you can run a benchmark script. We also provide a latency benchmarking checklist and sample harness.
[04:15] Samir: What's the rate limit on the trial? Will we be throttled for repeated requests?
[04:20] Ava: Trials have reasonable quotas to prevent abuse; if you need a higher QPS for benching we can temporarily increase it for the pilot. Just tell us expected QPS and burst.
[04:31] Priya: About logs and retention — audit logs at token level, or aggregated?
[04:36] Diego: We can provide request-level logs for enterprise plans. For PLG hosted trial it's aggregated, but we can enable more detailed logs on Dedicated or as an add-on. We also support configurable retention windows.
[04:55] Lena: How are costs measured? Tokens only or compute plus tokens?
[04:59] Ava: For hosted API it's per-token pricing; for Dedicated you pay for reserved capacity plus a lower per-token or usage charge depending on the contract. Optimize features like caching and batching reduce per-token effective cost.
[05:15] Samir: Any tips to get lower latency for chat-style sessions? We use KV cache heavily.
[05:20] Diego: Yes, use prefix caching, KV cache support, and shorter context windows; our runtime optimizes KV cache handling. There's also quantized model variants that reduce latency/cost at slight quality tradeoff. We'll point you to recommended configs.
[05:36] Lena: For SDKs, does the Node lib support streaming and function calling?
[05:40] Diego: Yes, streaming and tool/function calling are supported in both Python and Node SDKs. The console also shows example function schemas.
[05:48] Priya: On SSO, do you support SAML and SCIM provisioning?
[05:52] Ava: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in enterprise plans. For PLG orgs you can invite users but full SSO setup is part of enterprise onboarding.
[06:05] Samir: Ok, if we sign up today, what's the fastest path to get an engineer running inference?
[06:10] Diego: Sign up, verify domain, we provision credits, set API key — engineer clones quickstart repo, installs SDK, set API_KEY and run example. Typical dev feedback loop is minutes to <15 minutes.
[06:22] Lena: Is there a sandbox model with zero cost for dev iteration?
[06:26] Ava: We have small free credits or a tiny sandbox model with very limited QPS. Usually we give credits so you can run real tests.
[06:33] Priya: About compliance — are you able to sign data processing addendums and support contractual clauses for data residency?
[06:39] Ava: Yes, for enterprise contracts we sign DPAs and can discuss data residency and region restrictions. Hosted in specific regions can help with residency. Private on-prem is available for strict requirements.
[06:53] Samir: For the pilot, what's a reasonable scope? We're thinking endpoint chat and a reranker for search.
[06:59] Diego: That sounds good. For pilot, pick 2-3 routes: chat (low-latency path), rerank (batch scoring), and maybe embeddings. We'll provision test keys and monitor costs and latency.
[07:13] Lena: Do you support model version pinning in hosted?
[07:16] Diego: Yes, you can pin model versions in your route config; for hosted we keep compatible variants and give rollback options.
[07:24] Priya: Any known limitations with VPC peering?
[07:27] Diego: VPC peering for Private is common; for hosted we use secure endpoints and VPNs are possible via partners. For private deployments we do direct network integration.
[07:38] Samir: Are there rate-limited error codes we should handle?
[07:41] Diego: Yes, standard 429 for throttling, 503 for capacity issues. We recommend exponential backoff and a fallback model variant for critical flows.
[07:51] Lena: How do you surface cost per route?
[07:54] Ava: Console shows per-route token breakdown, and you can tag routes for cost center attribution. The Console also has token-level cost insights and alerts.
[08:07] Samir: What telemetry do you provide for model regressions?
[08:11] Diego: We have quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. You can upload evaluation prompts and track metric drift.
[08:22] Priya: For the security doc, will you include a network diagram for hosted vs private?
[08:25] Ava: Yes, we'll include diagrams for hosted, dedicated, and private network topologies in the security pack.
[08:35] Lena: OK, what's the approximate cost for 100k tokens on hosted for the model you recommend?
[08:40] Ava: It depends on model; rough example: $0.40 - $2 per 1k tokens depending on model size. We'll include example pricing in the sheet.
[08:52] Samir: For the bench, can you help run an initial burst test?
[08:56] Diego: We can. For higher QPS temporary increases are possible; we'll coordinate during the pilot.
[09:05] Priya: Any legal hoops for trial?
[09:08] Ava: Minimal — trial TOS and standard privacy terms. For enterprise we handle DPAs/negotiation.
[09:17] Lena: Sounds good. Can we go ahead and create the trial?
[09:20] Ava: Yes, I'll create a trial org for mistral-labs@ and provision credits. Diego will share quickstart repo links and example harness.
[09:31] Samir: One more Q: how do you handle long-running contexts, like chat history larger than 8k tokens?
[09:36] Diego: We recommend summarization and selective contexting; our runtime also supports KV cache and we have guidance on strategies to manage long context. For very large contexts, consider retrieval-augmented generation.
[09:55] Priya: For KMS, which providers do you support?
[09:59] Ava: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and vendors that support standard key wrap. For Private we can integrate with HSMs. We'll include the compatibility matrix in the pack.
[10:12] Lena: Great. Any limits on model switching in hosted?
[10:16] Diego: You can route to different models per route; switching is straightforward but you should validate quality/regressions via the eval tooling.
[10:28] Samir: Ok thanks. We should aim to have the pilot scoped by next week.
[10:32] Ava: Agreed. I'll follow up with proposed pilot plan and dates.
[10:39] -- mid call aside, minor audio glitch --
[12:00] Diego: (walkthrough) here's the quickstart repo link: github.com/redwood/quickstart (note: example link in notes). Example Node snippet: const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); const res = await client.generate({ model: 'rwd-small-v1', input: 'Hello' });
[12:32] Samir: That helps. We'll try it in the next 48 hours.
[13:05] Priya: When you send the security pack, please include contact for SOC2 reviewer.
[13:10] Ava: Yep, we'll include the security contact.
[14:00] Lena: Last bit on rollout: if pilot looks good, how quickly can we move to dedicated?
[14:06] Ava: Typically a few weeks to a month depending on capacity and contract. We can fast-track for higher urgency.
[14:20] Samir: For analytics, can we export token-level usage to our BI?
[14:25] Diego: You can export usage logs and we have API endpoints for metrics. Console also has CSV exports.
[14:36] Priya: Ok let's recap next steps.
[14:40] Ava: Recap: I (Ava) will create trial org and allocate credits; Diego will send quickstart links and benchmark checklist; I will send security pack and pricing sheet; Samir will share sample workload and target QPS and Lena will confirm pilot goals.
[14:59] Lena: Yep, that works. Thanks all.
[15:05] Ava: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by end of week.
[15:10] -- call ends
